question.problem:
Find the general solution to the system of differential equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=2{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-6{x}_{1}(t)-3{x}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ -6 & -3\end{aligned}].$

- Since $A$ is lower-triangular, the eigenvalues are 

$$
{\lambda }_{1}=-3\,\text{and}\,{\lambda }_{2}=2.
$$

- Let's go through the process of finding the eigenvectors.

- For ${\lambda }_{1}=-3,$ we get 

$$
A-{\lambda }_{1}I=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ -6 & 0\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}=2,$ we get 

$$
A-{\lambda }_{2}I=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ -6 & -5\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -6\end{aligned}].$

Now, we write down the general solution to the given linear system of differential equations: 

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={c}_{1}{v}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}{v}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t} \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -6\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R\end{aligned}
$$
